hints.title: Unequal Part Sizing Distribution Obstacle
hints.text: Dividing length by k leaves remainders that must be allocated to earlier segments. How can modulo arithmetic help you decide which parts receive an extra node?

hints.title: Quotient and Remainder Partition Invariant
hints.text: Every part has size length // k, and the first length % k parts receive exactly one additional node.

hints.title: Segment Decoupling Procedure
hints.text: Compute total length N. Determine base_size = N // k and extra = N % k. For each part, compute target length = base_size + (1 if i < extra else 0). Traverse that many nodes, disconnect the tail link by setting tail.next = null, and record the segment head.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def splitListToParts(self, head: Optional[ListNode], k: int) -> list[Optional[ListNode]]:
        length = 0
        curr = head
        while curr:
            length += 1
            curr = curr.next
        base_size = length // k
        extra = length % k
        res = []
        curr = head
        for i in range(k):
            part_head = curr
            part_len = base_size + (1 if i < extra else 0)
            for _ in range(part_len - 1):
                if curr:
                    curr = curr.next
            if curr:
                nxt = curr.next
                curr.next = None
                curr = nxt
            res.append(part_head)
        return res
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Two passes: one to count length and one to decouple k segments.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Slicing without tracking the remainder produces segments with size differences greater than 1.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Decoupling node pointers directly avoids creating new node instances beyond the output pointer array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling k > N gracefully by padding remaining slots in the result with null.
